title: Transient corium stratification and heat focusing
open: Predict maximum vessel-wall heat loading while melt progressively arrives, incorporates structural material, and exchanges species between oxide and metal layers. Resolve whether transient stratification or inversion produces peaks missed by steady-state configurations.
status: Carénini et al. (2025) compared eight IAEA benchmark cases and documented remaining thermochemistry, heavy-metal-layer, debris-melting, and heat-transfer discrepancies after decades of retention research.
why: Demonstrating melt retention requires bounding transient heat loads.
key_works: L. Carénini et al. (2025), *IVMR modelling with transient effects during molten pool formation and stabilization—Outcomes from models’ comparison performed in the IAEA CRP J46002*, [DOI:10.1016/j.anucene.2025.111365](https://doi.org/10.1016/j.anucene.2025.111365).

title: Directional corium–concrete erosion
open: Predict the evolving split between lateral and downward concrete erosion from melt composition, concrete chemistry, gas generation, and crust structure. Validate across siliceous and carbonate-bearing concretes under dry and flooded conditions.
status: The MCCI programme and its 2017 synthesis established substantial integral evidence. Orientation-dependent erosion and extrapolation among compositions remain sources of uncertainty.
why: Erosion geometry determines cooling surfaces and progression of structural attack.
key_works: OECD NEA (2017), [*State-of-the-Art Report on Molten Corium Concrete Interaction and Ex-Vessel Molten Core Coolability*](https://cms.oecd-nea.org/jcms/pl_19746/state-of-the-art-report-on-molten-corium-concrete-interaction-and-ex-vessel-molten-core-coolability).

title: Recombiner performance in chemically complex atmospheres
open: Predict passive hydrogen-recombiner removal rates under mixed gases, aerosols, oxygen limitation, and catalyst poisoning. Validate degradation and recovery under changing accident atmospheres.
status: THEMIS completed targeted tests by 2023 and an integral aerosol–recombiner interaction test in 2024; mixture and exposure-history transfer remains open.
why: Catalytic mitigation must function in the chemically complex atmosphere it helps control.
key_works: OECD NEA and Becker Technologies (2020–2024), [*THAI Experiments on Mitigation measures… (THEMIS)*](https://oecd-nea.org/jcms/pl_58863/thai-experiments-on-mitigation-measures-and-source-term-issues-to-support-analysis-and-further-improvement-of-severe-accident-management-measures-themis-project).

title: Organic iodine from aged containment surfaces
open: Predict organic-iodine formation and destruction from aged paints and other surfaces under irradiation, humidity changes, and chemical contamination. Separate surface-layer, pore, and bulk-water reactions sufficiently to transfer kinetics among coatings.
status: BIP phases through 2019 measured adsorption, desorption, and organic-iodide production. Paint aging and confident reactor-scale extrapolation remained explicit programme targets.
why: Organic iodine can be harder to retain than other iodine forms.
key_works: OECD NEA and Canadian Nuclear Laboratories (2007–2019), [*Behaviour of Iodine Project (BIP)*](https://oecd-nea.org/jcms/pl_24819/behaviour-of-iodine-project-bip).

title: Species-resolved aerosol pool scrubbing
open: Predict retention for aerosol sizes and chemical forms as bubbles rise during transients. Couple breakup, hygroscopic growth, dissolution, and re-entrainment, validating beyond an aggregate decontamination factor.
status: THEMIS completed pool-scrubbing experiments and a benchmark by its 2024 closeout; transfer among mixtures, bubble populations, and evolving chemistry remains incomplete.
why: The least-retained fraction can dominate airborne activity.
key_works: OECD NEA and Becker Technologies (2020–2024), [*THAI Experiments on Mitigation measures… (THEMIS)*](https://oecd-nea.org/jcms/pl_58863/thai-experiments-on-mitigation-measures-and-source-term-issues-to-support-analysis-and-further-improvement-of-severe-accident-management-measures-themis-project).

title: Gas-fast-reactor heat removal after depressurization
subfield: Integrated reactor systems and power conversion
open: Demonstrate reliable decay-heat removal for a gas-cooled fast reactor after simultaneous pressure loss and loss of normal electrical support, accounting for realistic flow resistance and degraded equipment.
status: A central GFR issue since the 2002 Generation IV roadmap. ALLEGRO analyses and experiments have advanced; Bali and Mayer’s 2025 investigation supplies a recent partial result.
why: Determines whether the fast-spectrum helium concept can satisfy its safety case.
key_works: Stainsby et al. (2009), *Gas Cooled Fast Reactor Research and Development in the European Union*, [DOI:10.1155/2009/238624](https://doi.org/10.1155/2009/238624); Bali and Mayer (2025), [*Investigation of decay heat removal systems in the ALLEGRO helium-cooled fast reactor*](https://www.sciencedirect.com/science/article/pii/S0029549325001293).

title: Quantifying digital common-cause failure
subfield: Monitoring, control, operations, and probabilistic safety
open: Estimate defensible failure bounds for diverse digital protection channels sharing specifications, tools, suppliers, or development assumptions. Validate whether proposed diversity measures predict actual independence.
status: NRC’s 2010 diversity-strategy report provides architectures and assessment foundations. Credible quantitative probabilities for rare shared software defects remain unresolved.
why: Prevents nominal redundancy from overstating reliability.
key_works: Wood et al. (2010), [*Diversity Strategies for Nuclear Power Plant Instrumentation and Control Systems*](https://www.ornl.gov/publication/diversity-strategies-nuclear-power-plant-instrumentation-and-control-systems-0), NUREG/CR-7007.

title: Safe industrial-heat interfaces across plant boundaries
subfield: Electricity systems, industrial heat, hydrogen, and water
open: Qualify interfaces isolating nuclear heat sources from industrial chemical hazards while tolerating rapid demand changes. Demonstrate that process-plant upsets preserve reactor protection assumptions.
status: HTTR experience and JAEA’s 2020 cogeneration work establish design and licensing foundations. Broader industrial integration requires application-specific validation and commercial demonstration.
why: Enables nuclear steam and high-temperature heat for manufacturing.
key_works: Sato, Aoki, Ohashi, and Yan (2020), [*Research and development for safety and licensing of HTGR cogeneration system*](https://www.sciencedirect.com/science/article/abs/pii/S0029549319305242).

title: Accelerator availability for subcritical power systems
subfield: Space, marine systems, research reactors, and accelerator-driven systems
open: Demonstrate an accelerator-driven civilian system whose beam interruptions, recovery, target lifetime, and thermal cycling permit sustained useful operation. Verify integrated availability over a representative campaign.
status: Pursued for decades. MYRRHA’s staged accelerator work emphasizes reliability, and EU programmes have compared requirements with operating evidence; complete availability demonstration remains open.
why: Determines whether transmutation and irradiation benefits survive interruptions and maintenance.
key_works: SCK CEN, [*MYRRHA linear accelerator*](https://www.myrrha.be/about-myrrha/myrrha-linear-accelerator); EU MAX consortium (2011–2014), [*MYRRHA Accelerator eXperiment*](https://cordis.europa.eu/project/id/269565/reporting).

title: High-burnup cladding after decades of thermal history
open: Predict residual ductility and fracture resistance after realistic drying, cooling, and storage histories. Validate blind predictions across cladding alloys against aged irradiated material.
status: NWTRB’s 2021 review identified representativeness and integration gaps. Short specimens and accelerated histories provide incomplete long-term validation.
why: Supports justified storage extensions and later handling.
key_works: NWTRB (2021), [*Evaluation of the Department of Energy’s Research Program to Examine the Performance of Commercial High Burnup Spent Nuclear Fuel During Extended Storage and Transportation*](https://www.nwtrb.gov/our-work/reports/evaluation-of-the-department-of-energy's-research-program-to-examine-the-performance-of-commercial-high-burnup-spent-nuclear-fuel-during-extended-storage-and-transportation-(july-2021)).

title: Site-specific canister corrosion forecasting
open: Forecast chloride deposition, wetting, pit initiation, and crack-growth distributions from site weather and measured canister surfaces. Demonstrate calibrated remaining-life predictions across coastal and inland installations.
status: Laboratory mechanisms and deposition models exist. Suffield et al.’s 2023 report, posted in 2024, developed heated-canister deposition modeling while describing coastal field demonstration as prospective.
why: Enables evidence-based inspection intervals and targeted maintenance.
key_works: S. R. Suffield et al. (2023), [*Thermal and Deposition Modeling Update for the Canister Deposition Field Demonstration*](https://www.pnnl.gov/publications/thermal-and-deposition-modeling-update-canister-deposition-field-demonstration), PNNL-34772.

title: Valid acceleration of waste-glass durability tests
open: Determine which accelerated conditions preserve mechanisms governing long-term glass release. Establish transfer rules and uncertainty bounds connecting tests, natural analogues, and repository conditions for specified glass families.
status: Standard methods date to the 1980s. Thorpe et al. (2021) document methodological progress and composition-dependent responses; a universal acceleration factor remains unjustified.
why: Accelerates qualification while preserving relevant chemistry.
key_works: C. L. Thorpe et al. (2021), *Forty Years of Durability Assessment of Nuclear Waste Glass by Standard Methods*, [DOI:10.1038/s41529-021-00210-4](https://doi.org/10.1038/s41529-021-00210-4).

title: Dilatant gas migration through clay barriers
open: Predict gas breakthrough, pathway creation, resealing, and coupled water movement under realistic clay-barrier stress histories. Reproduce independent laboratory and large-scale experiments without retuning mechanisms for each test.
status: DECOVALEX-2019 compared modeling approaches; DECOVALEX-2023 Task B extended work toward larger experiments. Gas-pathway transferability remains unresolved.
why: Constrains pressure and transport effects of repository-generated gases.
key_works: DECOVALEX (2019–2023), [*DECOVALEX-2023 Task B: Gas Transport in Clay*](https://decovalex.org/past-phases/D-2023/task-b).

title: Seawater uranium recovery with favourable full lifecycle performance
open: Demonstrate sustained recovery with favorable material lifetime, regeneration, energy use, marine impacts, and full costs at a stated scale. Report complete balances from repeated real-seawater operation.
status: Investigated for decades. Abney et al.’s 2017 review documents adsorbent and marine-testing progress; industrial lifecycle performance remains beyond laboratory uptake capacity.
why: Could diversify resources while establishing actual environmental tradeoffs.
key_works: C. W. Abney, R. T. Mayes, T. Saito, and S. Dai (2017), *Materials for the Recovery of Uranium from Seawater*, [DOI:10.1021/acs.chemrev.7b00355](https://doi.org/10.1021/acs.chemrev.7b00355).

title: Convergent selection of fission collective coordinates
open: Establish an error-controlled rule for choosing deformation, neck, pairing, and intrinsic coordinates in a reduced fission calculation. Demonstrate convergence of observable distributions when omitted coordinates are restored.
status: The issue predates modern density-functional calculations and remains explicit in the 2020 fission-theory roadmap. Successful fits using a few coordinates do not establish that the reduction preserves all relevant branches.
why: An adequacy criterion would distinguish physical predictions from artifacts of a chosen shape space.
key_works: M. Bender et al. (2020), *Future of Nuclear Fission Theory*, [arXiv:2005.10216](https://arxiv.org/abs/2005.10216).

title: Microscopic capture–fission branching without phenomenological widths
open: Calculate competition between neutron capture and fission from microscopic many-body states with a common normalization, reproducing branching ratios across an energy interval. Identify which missing configurations or interactions dominate discrepancies.
status: Uzawa and Hagino’s 2025 nonequilibrium Green-function calculation added proton–neutron interactions and relaxed a seniority restriction, but still underestimated the experimental fission-to-capture branching ratio by about an order of magnitude.
why: Tests whether reaction probabilities can emerge from microscopic dynamics rather than independently fitted channel widths.
key_works: K. Uzawa and K. Hagino (2025), *A microscopic calculation of fission cross sections with the non-equilibrium Green function method*, [arXiv:2504.01572](https://arxiv.org/abs/2504.01572).

title: Converged microscopic joint fragment distributions
open: Predict the joint distribution of fragment charge, mass, and total kinetic energy, including covariances and rare branches, with demonstrable convergence in the number of microscopic trajectories. Validate reactions excluded from calibration.
status: Li et al. (2025) coherently combined 25 time-dependent trajectories for a realistic fission application. This advances beyond mean trajectories but does not establish convergence for all joint observables.
why: Marginal distributions can agree while correlations needed for radiation predictions remain wrong.
key_works: B. Li et al. (2025), *Microscopic model for yields and total kinetic energy in nuclear fission*, [DOI:10.1103/PhysRevC.111.L051302](https://doi.org/10.1103/PhysRevC.111.L051302).

title: Observable-independent definition of nuclear scission
open: Define separation into fragments so that predicted masses, excitation energies, and interactions converge independently of arbitrary neck-density thresholds. Reconcile localization-based and dynamical definitions in benchmark calculations.
status: Younes and Gogny’s 2011 quantum-localization treatment clarified separation of fragment wave functions. A universally validated prescription spanning static, collective, and real-time calculations has not followed.
why: A shifting scission surface can change inferred fragment properties even with the same underlying nuclear state.
key_works: W. Younes and D. Gogny (2011), *Nuclear Scission and Quantum Localization*, [DOI:10.1103/PhysRevLett.107.132501](https://doi.org/10.1103/PhysRevLett.107.132501).

title: Experimental separation of scission neutrons
open: Isolate neutrons associated with neck rupture from evaporation by accelerated fragments, with an experimentally constrained spectrum and angular distribution. Demonstrate that the inferred component survives alternative detector-response and fragment-emission models.
status: The mechanism has been debated for decades. Abdurrahman et al. (2023) supplied microscopic neck-rupture and scission-neutron predictions; discriminating experimental extraction remains the relevant open test.
why: Unresolved components bias interpretation of prompt-neutron spectra and correlations.
key_works: I. Abdurrahman, M. Kafker, A. Bulgac, and I. Stetcu (2023), *Neck Rupture and Scission Neutrons in Nuclear Fission*, [arXiv:2307.13132](https://arxiv.org/abs/2307.13132).

title: Genuine three-heavy-fragment fission probability
open: Establish whether reported collinear tripartition into three medium-mass fragments is a reproducible nuclear channel, and determine its probability or robust upper limits. Exclude binary-fission backgrounds and detector ambiguities through independent coincidence measurements.
status: The channel remains disputed. Jaganathen and Skalski (2025) predict strong dynamical suppression, with model-dependent upper estimates around \(10^{-8}\)–\(10^{-11}\) per binary decay for studied systems; this is not an impossibility proof.
why: Tests how nuclei choose among competing fragmentation topologies.
key_works: Y. Jaganathen and J. Skalski (2025), *Suppression of genuine tripartition in heavy nuclei: A self-consistent perspective*, [arXiv:2506.22534](https://arxiv.org/abs/2506.22534).
aliases: Collinear cluster tripartition; genuine ternary fission.

title: Fragment excitation sharing and quantum entanglement
open: Predict the fragment-mass dependence and fluctuations of excitation-energy sharing, and identify measurements distinguishing entanglement-based descriptions from statistical alternatives. Reproduce neutron-multiplicity trends without empirical energy-partition functions.
status: Energy-sharing prescriptions remain model dependent. Qiang, Pei, and Godbey (2024) connected microscopic entanglement to the observed sawtooth structure, while showing that additional fluctuations affect predicted slopes.
why: Excitation sharing controls which fragment emits neutrons and how much gamma energy follows.
key_works: Y. Qiang, J. Pei, and K. Godbey (2024), *Quantum Entanglement in Nuclear Fission*, [arXiv:2408.07375](https://arxiv.org/abs/2408.07375).

title: Origin of primordial fragment angular momentum
open: Determine when and through which collective or microscopic modes fragment spins are generated. Find observables discriminating independent spin generation from correlated pre-scission dynamics before evaporation obscures the difference.
status: Wilson et al. (2021) measured weak final-spin correlations, motivating a post-scission interpretation. Microscopic calculations continue to investigate different primordial correlations; measured final distributions do not uniquely fix the mechanism.
why: Fragment spins shape gamma cascades and isomer production.
key_works: J. N. Wilson et al. (2021), *Angular momentum generation in nuclear fission*, [DOI:10.1038/s41586-021-03304-w](https://doi.org/10.1038/s41586-021-03304-w).

title: Reconstructing pre-emission fragment spin correlations
open: Infer primordial fragment-spin correlations from neutron and gamma coincidences using decay models with independently constrained uncertainties. Establish which correlations are identifiable and which are erased by unobserved emissions.
status: Stetcu et al. (2021) showed substantial angular-momentum removal during fragment decay. Interpreting final gamma observables as direct primordial-spin measurements therefore remains an unresolved inverse problem.
why: Reliable inversion is needed to adjudicate competing fission-spin mechanisms.
key_works: I. Stetcu et al. (2021), *Angular Momentum Removal by Neutron and γ-Ray Emissions during Fission Fragment Decays*, [arXiv:2108.04347](https://arxiv.org/abs/2108.04347).

title: Odd–even yield staggering across excitation and odd nuclei
open: Predict how charge and neutron-number staggering evolves with excitation energy, including quasiparticle blocking and broken-pair configurations. Reproduce isotope-resolved yields across even and odd fissioning nuclei without empirical staggering factors.
status: Verriere, Regnier, and Schunck (2021) demonstrated recovery of charge staggering using particle-number projection. Systematic combination with realistic odd-system dynamics and excitation dependence remains incomplete.
why: Fine yield structure affects individual radionuclide inventories and decay emissions.
key_works: M. Verriere, D. Regnier, and N. Schunck (2021), *Microscopic Calculation of Fission Product Yields with Particle Number Projection*, [arXiv:2102.02346](https://arxiv.org/abs/2102.02346).

title: Uranium-238 state-resolved inelastic-scattering closure
subfield: Nuclear reaction, fission-yield, and decay data
open: Determine the 238U inelastic cross section by consistently combining observed gamma transitions, unobserved cascades, and direct neutron measurements. Close the gap between state-specific measurements and the total channel with documented covariance.
status: A high-priority request has existed since 2008. Kerveno et al. (2021) supplied extensive neutron-induced gamma data; incomplete level schemes and reaction-model dependence still complicate reconstruction.
why: Uranium inelastic scattering changes fast-neutron spectra and interpretation of irradiations.
key_works: M. Kerveno et al. (2021), *Measurement of 238U(n,n′γ) cross section data and their impact on reaction models*, [DOI:10.1103/PhysRevC.104.044605](https://doi.org/10.1103/PhysRevC.104.044605); OECD NEA, [HPRL request](https://cms.oecd-nea.org/jcms/pl_68811/92-u-238-n-inl).

title: Plutonium-239 capture normalization across energy regimes
subfield: Nuclear reaction, fission-yield, and decay data
open: Reconcile resonance-region and fast-energy 239Pu capture measurements within a joint capture–fission evaluation retaining shared normalization uncertainties. Demonstrate agreement with independent measurements without separate energy-dependent adjustments that conceal discrepancies.
status: Mosby et al. (2018) provided a unifying capture measurement from keV to MeV energies. The NEA capture request remains active; improved coverage has not eliminated evaluation and normalization questions.
why: Capture competition influences isotope evolution and neutron balances in civilian fuel calculations.
key_works: S. Mosby et al. (2018), *Unifying measurement of 239Pu(n,γ) in the keV to MeV energy regime*, [DOI:10.1103/PhysRevC.97.041601](https://doi.org/10.1103/PhysRevC.97.041601).

title: Independently replicated plutonium-241 capture data
subfield: Nuclear reaction, fission-yield, and decay data
open: Complete analysis and independent replication of 241Pu neutron-capture measurements, then establish a covariance-bearing evaluation resolving dependence on the historical dataset. Test compatibility with simultaneously measured competing channels.
status: Weston and Todd’s 1978 work long dominated direct capture information. CEA reported new measurements undergoing analysis in 2026; acquiring data is therefore already a partial result.
why: Sparse capture data limit isotope-inventory predictions involving 241Pu.
key_works: L. W. Weston and J. H. Todd (1978), *Neutron Capture and Fission Cross Sections of Plutonium-241*, [DOI:10.13182/NSE78-A27176](https://doi.org/10.13182/NSE78-A27176); CEA (2026), [*Experimental challenges of nuclear reactions on plutonium-241*](https://irfu.cea.fr/en/Phocea/Vie_des_labos/Ast/ast.php?id_ast=5474&t=fait_marquant).

title: Americium-241 fast-energy capture uncertainty
subfield: Nuclear reaction, fission-yield, and decay data
open: Reduce uncertainty in 241Am capture across fast-energy ranges identified by sensitivity studies, using consistent differential measurements and evaluation. Demonstrate improvement under independent validation, including normalization correlations.
status: An established NEA priority before the 2018 n_TOF publication. The thermal-data component was completed in May 2022; the request leaves the fast-energy component in progress.
why: The remaining gap affects inventories and irradiation predictions for americium-bearing civilian materials.
key_works: E. Mendoza et al. (2018), *Measurement and analysis of the 241Am neutron capture cross section at the n_TOF facility at CERN*, [DOI:10.1103/PhysRevC.97.054616](https://doi.org/10.1103/PhysRevC.97.054616); OECD NEA, [HPRL status](https://cms.oecd-nea.org/jcms/pl_68808/95-am-241-n-g-n-tot).

title: Consistent gadolinium-155 and gadolinium-157 resonance evaluations
subfield: Nuclear reaction, fission-yield, and decay data
open: Produce capture and transmission evaluations for 155Gd and 157Gd that jointly reproduce modern experiments and resolve discrepant thermal values. Meet the requested roughly 4% accuracy with independently validated covariance.
status: NEA requests were submitted in 2018. Mastromarco et al. (2019) supplied thermal and epithermal measurements; subsequent work concerns evaluation and validation rather than wholly unmeasured reactions.
why: These isotopes strongly influence gadolinium neutron-absorber behavior.
key_works: M. Mastromarco et al. (2019), *Cross section measurements of 155,157Gd(n,γ) induced by thermal and epithermal neutrons*, [DOI:10.1140/epja/i2019-12692-7](https://doi.org/10.1140/epja/i2019-12692-7); OECD NEA, [request status](https://cms.oecd-nea.org/jcms/pl_68888/64-gd-155-n-g-n-tot).

title: Iron-56 inelastic neutron–gamma channel closure
subfield: Nuclear reaction, fission-yield, and decay data
open: Reconcile 56Fe outgoing-neutron spectra, level-specific gamma production, and total inelastic scattering over the fast-energy range. Identify missing transitions or reaction-model ingredients and publish a common covariance evaluation.
status: A NEA high-priority request has remained active since 2008. The 2018 CIELO evaluation improved iron modeling; state-resolved measurements and channel consistency remain active work.
why: Iron is ubiquitous in structural materials, shielding, and neutron diagnostics.
key_works: M. Herman et al. (2018), [*Evaluation of Neutron Reactions on Iron Isotopes for CIELO and ENDF/B-VIII.0*](https://www.ornl.gov/publication/evaluation-neutron-reactions-iron-isotopes-cielo-and-endfb-viii0); OECD NEA, [High Priority Request List](https://www.oecd-nea.org/jcms/pl_68746/hprlapp).

title: Early-time decay heat with separate beta and gamma benchmarks
subfield: Nuclear reaction, fission-yield, and decay data
open: Obtain independent pulse-irradiation decay-heat benchmarks separately resolving electron and electromagnetic energy at short cooling times. Identify specific decay-data errors responsible for disagreements instead of validating only total heat.
status: Historical measurements and summation evaluations provide substantial coverage. Nichols et al. (2023) review persistent priorities; agreement in total power can conceal opposite beta and gamma errors.
why: Radiation components deposit energy over different distances and need separate predictions.
key_works: A. L. Nichols et al. (2023), *Improving fission-product decay data for reactor applications: part I—decay heat*, [DOI:10.1140/epja/s10050-023-00969-x](https://doi.org/10.1140/epja/s10050-023-00969-x).

title: Directly isolated uranium-238 antineutrino spectrum
open: Determine the 238U fast-fission antineutrino spectrum with substantially reduced conversion and isotope-mixture dependence, especially at high energy. Require direct isolation or demonstrably identifiable multi-source inference with published covariance.
status: Haag et al. (2014) measured electrons and converted their spectrum, with increasing uncertainty at high energy. A complementary direct-neutrino determination and improved precision remain open.
why: The smaller 238U contribution can still influence the high-energy reactor spectrum.
key_works: N. Haag et al. (2014), *Experimental Determination of the Antineutrino Spectrum of the Fission Products of 238U*, [arXiv:1312.5601](https://arxiv.org/abs/1312.5601).

title: Reactor antineutrino spectrum below inverse-beta threshold
open: Reconstruct the reactor antineutrino spectrum below approximately 1.8 MeV with calibrated response, background control, and uncertainty independent of assumed summation spectra. Establish which features are identifiable through recoil measurements.
status: Standard inverse-beta measurements cannot access this region. CONUS+ observed reactor coherent scattering in 2025, but an integrated recoil excess does not determine the full subthreshold source spectrum.
why: Exposes a large, weakly tested part of reactor beta-decay emission.
key_works: N. Ackermann et al. (2025), *Direct observation of coherent elastic antineutrino–nucleus scattering*, [DOI:10.1038/s41586-025-09322-2](https://doi.org/10.1038/s41586-025-09322-2).

title: Correlation-aware criticality tallies
subfield: Reactor physics, transport, and computational verification
open: Produce local power estimates and confidence intervals that remain calibrated in large, weakly coupled reactor models despite source clustering and population control. Demonstrate coverage across independent calculations, including spatially undersampled regions.
status: A decades-old Monte Carlo difficulty. Fröhlicher et al. demonstrated generational variance reduction on a one-speed slab in 2023; general reactor-scale guarantees remain a research target.
why: Prevents apparently precise calculations from concealing local statistical bias.
key_works: Fröhlicher et al. (2023), *Generational variance reduction in Monte Carlo criticality simulations as a way of mitigating unwanted correlations*, [arXiv:2301.03882](https://arxiv.org/abs/2301.03882).

title: Affordable fully transient Monte Carlo
subfield: Reactor physics, transport, and computational verification
open: Reduce computation for continuous-energy, three-dimensional reactor transients by at least tenfold against a declared reference, retaining independently verified time-resolved uncertainty and delayed-neutron dynamics. This is a proposed performance target.
status: Fully transient simulation exists. MC/DC’s 2024 release and 2023 initial-particle sampling methods supply baselines; coupled, long-duration transients remain expensive.
why: Makes independent transient reference solutions practical for routine validation.
key_works: Morgan et al. (2024), *Monte Carlo / Dynamic Code (MC/DC): An accelerated Python package for fully transient neutron transport and rapid methods development*, [DOI:10.21105/joss.06415](https://doi.org/10.21105/joss.06415); Variansyah et al. (2023), *An effective initial particle sampling technique for Monte Carlo reactor transient simulations*, [arXiv:2305.07646](https://arxiv.org/abs/2305.07646).

title: Positive, conservative adaptive low-rank transport
subfield: Reactor physics, transport, and computational verification
open: Develop adaptive low-rank neutron transport preserving nonnegative flux and particle balance, with usable error bounds through streaming, sharp material interfaces, and transient rank growth.
status: Kusch et al. established a low-rank criticality iteration and simplified convergence analysis in 2022. Savings are demonstrated; the combined guarantees over realistic heterogeneous transients remain unestablished.
why: Reduces memory without sacrificing physically meaningful solutions.
key_works: Kusch, Whewell, McClarren, and Frank (2022), *A low-rank power iteration scheme for neutron transport criticality problems*, [arXiv:2201.12340](https://arxiv.org/abs/2201.12340).

title: Nonlinear uncertainty through depletion histories
subfield: Reactor physics, transport, and computational verification
open: Propagate correlated nuclear-data, flux, composition, and operating-history uncertainties through repeated irradiation and cooling without uncontrolled linearization. Validate residual-heat and isotope-inventory uncertainty against held-out assays.
status: Diez et al. (2015) showed that approximation choices and covariance libraries materially change burn-up uncertainty. Full sampling supplies a costly baseline; efficient reliable nonlinear propagation remains open.
why: Supports defensible fuel, storage, and waste predictions.
key_works: Diez et al. (2015), *Comparison of nuclear data uncertainty propagation methodologies for PWR burn-up simulations*, [DOI:10.1016/j.anucene.2014.10.022](https://doi.org/10.1016/j.anucene.2014.10.022).

title: Identifiability limits of neutron-noise diagnosis
subfield: Reactor physics, transport, and computational verification
open: Characterize combinations of core vibration, coolant fluctuations, and detector drift that are indistinguishable from a finite noisy detector set. Prove bounds or construct experiments separating ambiguous causes.
status: CORTEX developed methods and controlled-reactor experiments during 2017–2021. The requested identifiability map is a proposed extension, rather than an existing named theorem.
why: Establishes when localization is supported by evidence and when additional sensors are needed.
key_works: Demazière et al. (2017), [*Noise-based core monitoring and diagnostics—Overview of the CORTEX project*](https://research.chalmers.se/en/publication/253656).

title: Origin of bimodal intragranular gas bubbles
open: Determine which combination of nucleation, dislocation trapping, coalescence, and irradiation-driven gas removal creates the two observed nanometre-scale bubble populations in UO₂. Predict both distributions across temperature and fission rate without separately fitting each irradiation.
status: A decades-old microstructure question. A 2025 phase-field study reproduced bimodality using gas re-solution, but alternative mechanisms remain experimentally distinguishable.
why: Bubble populations control swelling, gas retention, and subsequent fragmentation.
key_works: Jiajun Zhao et al. (2025), *Mesoscale simulation on bimodal distribution of nano-sized intragranular fission bubbles in UO₂*, [journal article](https://www.sciencedirect.com/science/article/abs/pii/S0167577X24019591).

title: Fission-spike gas re-solution law
open: Establish a transferable rate law for fission-fragment tracks returning xenon from bubbles to the fuel matrix, including bubble size, track offset, energy deposition, and nearby dislocations. Use independent gas inventories to distinguish thermal-spike and ballistic mechanisms.
status: Setyawan et al. parameterized atomistic re-solution in 2018. Conversion of electronic deposition into atomic heating remains a source of uncertainty in engineering-scale rates.
why: Incorrect re-solution rates propagate into swelling and gas-release predictions.
key_works: W. Setyawan et al. (2018), *Atomistic model of xenon gas bubble re-solution rate due to thermal spike in uranium oxide*, [DOI:10.1063/1.5042770](https://doi.org/10.1063/1.5042770).

title: Transient burst fission-gas release
open: Predict rapid gas release during power changes from measured pre-transient microstructure, including grain-face crack opening and healing. Reproduce timing and quantity in withheld transients where ordinary diffusion contributes little.
status: Burst release has long resisted purely diffusional treatments. NEA’s dedicated benchmark isolates short transients to distinguish the mechanism from slower diffusion.
why: Bursts alter internal pressure and fuel–cladding heat transfer during transients.
key_works: OECD NEA, [*Burst Fission Gas Release Benchmark of the Expert Group on Reactor Fuel Performance*](https://oecd-nea.org/jcms/pl_70791/burst-fission-gas-release-fgr-benchmark-of-the-expert-group-on-reactor-fuel-performance-egrfp).

title: Separating grain-size and diffusivity benefits of doped fuel
open: Quantify when larger grains improve gas retention enough to offset dopant-induced changes in xenon diffusivity. Use matched irradiations varying grain size and chemical state independently, predicting steady release and transient response.
status: Cooper et al. (2021) connected atomistic chemistry to engineering gas-release models. Competing effects motivate dedicated separate-effects irradiation studies.
why: Qualification requires causal evidence for improved performance under particular conditions.
key_works: M. W. D. Cooper et al. (2021), *Fission gas diffusion and release for Cr₂O₃-doped UO₂: From the atomic to the engineering scale*, [DOI:10.1016/j.jnucmat.2020.152590](https://doi.org/10.1016/j.jnucmat.2020.152590).

title: Metallic-fuel chemical attack of cladding
open: Predict chemically weakened cladding depth from interfacial layers, transported fission products, and temperature history. Test predictions at intermediate conditions and along full-length irradiated pins.
status: Salvato et al. (2024) compared two irradiated conditions and obtained useful model agreement, while identifying missing intermediate-condition and prototypic-length evidence.
why: Chemical attack can limit fuel lifetime even when bulk swelling is acceptable.
key_works: D. Salvato et al. (2024), *The effect of temperature and burnup on U-10Zr metallic fuel chemical interaction with HT-9: A SEM-EDS study*, [DOI:10.1016/j.jnucmat.2024.154928](https://doi.org/10.1016/j.jnucmat.2024.154928).

title: Silver transport through apparently intact silicon carbide
open: Determine the relative roles of grain boundaries, nanopore trapping, irradiation defects, and chemically assisted pathways in silver escape through intact TRISO silicon carbide. Predict release across independently characterized coating microstructures.
status: An enduring coated-fuel puzzle. AbdulHameed et al.’s 2025 preprint required nanopore trapping to reconcile a grain-boundary transport model with measurements.
why: Silver release creates contamination and maintenance burdens despite otherwise effective containment.
key_works: M. AbdulHameed et al. (2025), *Modeling of silver transport in cubic SiC: Integrating molecular dynamics, bounds averaging, and uncertainty quantification*, [arXiv:2508.14325](https://arxiv.org/abs/2508.14325).

title: TRISO failure probabilities in the extreme tail
open: Predict rare particle failures from joint distributions of coating geometry, defects, properties, and irradiation history. Validate correlated defects and non-spherical damage without inferring arbitrarily small failure rates from small zero-failure samples.
status: Jiang et al. (2021) implemented statistical failure analysis and multidimensional corrections in BISON. Population-tail validation beyond tested configurations remains open.
why: Whole-core retention depends on rare failures among enormous particle populations.
key_works: W. Jiang et al. (2021), *TRISO particle fuel performance and failure analysis with BISON*, [DOI:10.1016/j.jnucmat.2021.152795](https://doi.org/10.1016/j.jnucmat.2021.152795).

title: Late-life manganese–nickel–silicon precipitation
open: Predict precipitation and hardening during extended vessel exposure when low flux, alloy composition, and thermal aging interact. Establish when accelerated irradiation reproduces surveillance-steel precipitates and embrittlement without empirical compensation.
status: Almirall et al. (2024) characterized nine commercial steels at extended-life fluences and tested models. Extrapolation across low-flux, long-duration histories remains a qualification problem.
why: These precipitates can change the usable lifetime of reactor vessels.
key_works: N. Almirall et al. (2024), *Irradiation microstructures and hardening in commercial nuclear reactor pressure vessel steels at high extended life fluence*, [primary article](https://www.sciencedirect.com/science/article/pii/S258915292400053X).

title: When irradiation accelerates or suppresses salt corrosion
open: Establish when irradiation increases, decreases, or leaves unchanged intergranular corrosion in molten salts. Separate defect-enhanced alloy transport from radiolysis and chemical-potential changes, validating the sign across radiation species and salt conditions.
status: Zhou et al. (2019) observed proton irradiation decelerating Ni–Cr corrosion, disproving a simple assumption that irradiation always worsens attack. General operating boundaries remain open.
why: Unirradiated corrosion tests may misrepresent in-reactor wall loss.
key_works: W. Zhou et al. (2019), *Proton Irradiation-Decelerated Intergranular Corrosion of Ni-Cr Alloys in Molten Salt*, [arXiv:1911.11798](https://arxiv.org/abs/1911.11798).

title: Irradiated silicon-carbide composite hermeticity
open: Maintain and predict gas tightness of complete SiC composite tubes and joints under heat flux, irradiation, and thermal cycling. Connect microcracks and joint damage to measured leakage and sealing-layer lifetime.
status: Koyanagi et al. (2024) found radial-heat-flux irradiation could compromise composite-tube hermeticity while tested monolithic tubes retained it. Mitigation requires lifecycle validation.
why: Mechanical strength alone does not establish fission-product containment.
key_works: T. Koyanagi et al. (2024), *Hermeticity of SiC/SiC composite and monolithic SiC tubes irradiated under radial high-heat flux*, [DOI:10.1016/j.jnucmat.2023.154784](https://doi.org/10.1016/j.jnucmat.2023.154784).

title: Graphite dimensional turnaround across grades
open: Predict irradiation-driven shrinkage, expansion turnaround, and creep for a new graphite grade from its initial pore and crystallite structure. Provide calibrated uncertainty beyond measured grades and dose ranges.
status: Dhulipala et al. (2025) calibrated four irradiated-property models across five grades, including model discrepancy. Out-of-grade and extended-dose prediction remains a stronger target.
why: Core geometry and load paths evolve with graphite dimensions and stiffness.
key_works: S. L. N. Dhulipala et al. (2025), *Bayesian calibration of irradiated graphite property models under high temperatures*, [DOI:10.1038/s41529-025-00710-7](https://doi.org/10.1038/s41529-025-00710-7).

title: Disturbance-wave control of intermittent dryout
open: Predict dry-patch formation and rewetting from disturbance-wave statistics in high-pressure annular steam–water flow with spacers and nonuniform heating. Transfer mechanisms between fluids and geometries without refitting local closures.
status: Morse et al. (2024) directly characterized intermittent dryout and proposed mechanistic models using a transparent refrigerant experiment. Reactor-condition transfer remains the narrower open problem.
why: Local dry patches determine temperature excursions before complete film disappearance.
key_works: R. W. Morse et al. (2024), *A new paradigm for the role of disturbance waves on film dryout and wall heat transfer in annular two-phase flow*, [DOI:10.1016/j.ijheatmasstransfer.2023.124812](https://doi.org/10.1016/j.ijheatmasstransfer.2023.124812).

title: Tenfold lower consumptive cooling water
subfield: Electricity systems, industrial heat, hydrogen, and water
open: Demonstrate tenfold lower annual consumptive cooling water per net megawatt-hour, with no more than 5% annual output loss and 10% total levelized generation-cost premium against a wet-cooled reference under the same climate and duty cycle. These are proposed combined targets.
status: Dry and hybrid cooling reduce water demand with cost and efficiency penalties. Existing adaptation studies establish the trade-off, not this combined performance target.
why: Broadens siting options and reduces drought competition for water.
key_works: Van Vliet et al. (2016), *Power-generation system vulnerability and adaptation to changes in climate and water resources*, [DOI:10.1038/nclimate2903](https://doi.org/10.1038/nclimate2903); IAEA (2024), [*Climate Change and Nuclear Power 2024*](https://www-pub.iaea.org/MTCD/Publications/PDF/PUB9048_web.pdf).

title: Subpercent predictive closure of uranium-235 antineutrino yield
open: Predict absolute 235U antineutrino yield to subpercent accuracy from independent fission and beta-decay data, consistently with direct neutrino and aggregate electron measurements. Resolve remaining normalization differences without fitting the target neutrino yield.
status: The historical flux anomaly motivated renewed work from 2011. Revised summation calculations improve agreement; Perissé et al. (2023) still find incompatibility with legacy aggregate beta spectra and data-dominated uncertainties.
why: Accurate absolute yields strengthen tests of neutrino properties and quantitative reactor monitoring.
key_works: L. Perissé et al. (2023), *A comprehensive revision of the summation method for the prediction of reactor antineutrino fluxes and spectra*, [arXiv:2304.14992](https://arxiv.org/abs/2304.14992).
